Weekly Diff 2026-11-23

⬛ Overview · 🟪 AI Agents · 🟦 AI Models & Labs · 🟧 AI Policy · 🟨 Data Engineering · ⬜ Weekly Diff · 🟫 Trends

Items: 376 | Sources: the pages of 2026-11-17 to 2026-11-23 | Written by claude-opus-5-5 | Text in italics is interpretation | Generated: 2026-11-23 07:21 UTC

OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol reached coding agents this week, and two agents made Sol their default selection. Several reports this week concerned prompts leaking from inference providers, including a Together AI notice to customers about prompts sent to its serverless inference service in June and July 2026. On the data side, Azure Databricks retired Gemini 3.6 Flash on 2026-11-19 and set further retirement dates, while Databricks and Snowflake changed several defaults.

GPT-6.2 in the coding agents

OpenRouter's listing calls GPT-6.2 Sol an upgrade to GPT-6.1 Sol, positioned below GPT-6.2 Astra in the series. Codex 0.171.0 added both models to its catalogs, with Sol as the default catalog selection. Pi v1.6.0 made GPT-6.2 Sol the default for its openai, azure and openai-codex providers instead of GPT-6.1 Sol, at the same price. It also notes that both models reject reasoning effort none and minimal, so thinking level off is unavailable.

Caching needed a fix. OpenCode v2.3.2 says GPT-6.2 models don't cache a system prompt sent in the Responses instructions field, so every step re-billed it as uncached input. OpenCode now sends that prompt as a leading developer message. By its own figure, uncached input per step on GitHub Copilot gpt-6.2-sol dropped from about 14,000 tokens to 3. Oh My Pi v19.1.0 now sends GPT-6.2 system prompts as leading developer messages through third-party Responses proxies.

Not every path works yet. An Oh My Pi issue reports GPT-6.2 Sol missing from its Codex model list and rejected with model_not_found, while the native Codex CLI works. The reporter writes that the cause is not established.

In OpenRouter's one-day snapshot of top models on 2026-11-22, openai/gpt-6.1-sol-20260929 fell to #19 from #10 the week before. tencent/hy4-flash-20261116 entered the table at #4 with 10.21T tokens.

Separately, an issue on Claude Code reports premium Team and Enterprise seats using up their limits about 3–5x faster on non-Fable models since roughly the week of 2026-11-09. The reporter says everyone in their organization on premium seats sees the same drop.

The OpenCode figure suggests that, for GPT-6.2, where a harness places the system prompt can decide most of the per-step input bill. Harnesses that pass it in instructions are worth checking. The GPT-6.1 Sol drop is a single day's figure, and whether GPT-6.2 takes over that traffic is worth watching.

Prompts leaking from inference providers

OpenRouter says it off-boarded three providers. It also removed 125 endpoints from Zero Data Retention eligibility and notified potentially affected customers, after canary token research on inference providers. In a separate write-up, Dragos says it seeded two million AI prompts with canary tokens. It reports finding three provider breaches, prompt theft and ignored Zero Data Retention settings.

The package supply chain also had an incident. Socket's write-up on agent-framework says compromised versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 on PyPI use .pth startup hooks to exfiltrate Azure, GitHub Actions and CI/CD credentials.

Disclosure timelines are also changing. Anthropic says frontier models have become much better at discovering vulnerabilities. It is shortening its disclosure window from 90 days to 30 days for high- and critical-severity issues, and to 45 days for all others. The new timelines apply to vulnerabilities reported on or after 2027-01-01.

This suggests Zero Data Retention eligibility is a per-endpoint status that can change while a client relies on it. For EU work built on it, the list of eligible endpoints is worth watching. From 2027, Anthropic's shorter windows would also leave maintainers less time between a report and its disclosure.

Retirements and changed defaults in data platforms

The Genie One MCP Beta endpoint at /api/2.0/mcp/genie reaches end of life on 2026-11-30, after which requests fail. Its replacement is the system.ai.genie_one_mcp MCP in Unity Gateway. Azure Databricks retires GPT-5 and GPT-5 mini on 2026-12-11 and recommends GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6.1 Terra as replacements.

Several query and streaming results will change:

  • array_contains: Starting on or after 2027-01-15, with ANSI mode enabled in Databricks Runtime 19 and above, array_contains will return NULL instead of false for a constant empty array and a NULL value. As a result, NOT array_contains will no longer match those rows.
  • Streaming watermarks: In Databricks Runtime 19, new streaming queries in real-time mode use real-time watermark propagation by default, so state is evicted sooner. Queries restarted from an existing checkpoint keep their original behavior.
  • Output policies: Model output policies now default to streaming evaluation, including existing policies, and released text can't be recalled. This feature is in Beta.
  • Snowflake dynamic tables: Snowflake's AUTO refresh mode for dynamic tables now resolves to ADAPTIVE instead of INCREMENTAL when the definition supports incremental refresh.

Dagster 1.13.31 also has a breaking change: its Claude Code plugin no longer reads DAGSTER_CLOUD_MCP_URL. Organizations in the EU region must add the EU server directly, or the plugin connects to the US server and authentication fails.

Several of these changes alter results without raising an error: a NULL in place of false, earlier state eviction, and streamed text that can't be recalled. Those are the changes a test suite is least likely to flag. The Dagster change is the one that directly affects EU-region setups.

EU and Dutch regulators

The Commission is collecting feedback on a draft template for a questionnaire. The template is meant to help certain deployers of high-risk AI systems prepare a fundamental rights impact assessment under Article 27 of the AI Act. For 2026-12-02, the AI Act timeline lists bans on sexual deepfakes and CSAM generators, and the end of the Art. 50(2) transition.

The Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens advises consumers against buying AI camera glasses for general use. In its own study of six such glasses, one wrongly said an ambulance was on its way during a simulated resuscitation. The AP also found security problems in the software.

Politico Europe reports that an Irish regulator stopped X from training AI with data gathered by agents. The regulator says it has significant concerns about personal data being collected by AI agents. In the Tweede Kamer, an amended motion asks for an inventory of what is needed to supervise the AI Act.

The Irish case and the AP study both concern data that agents or devices collect about people other than the user. This suggests that is where regulator attention fell this week for agent projects at EU clients.

NariQ is a trellis-coded post-training quantization method that calibrates on tokens the BF16 model generates during agent sessions. The truncated abstract gives no NariQ result.
  • In anthropics/skills, #2246 reports that mcp-builder's v1 Node streamable HTTP example listens on every interface with no Host validation. AI Agents 2026-11-17

⬛ Overview · 🟪 AI Agents · 🟦 AI Models & Labs · 🟧 AI Policy · 🟨 Data Engineering

Projects: 15 | Active today: 5 | Stable releases: 7 | Prereleases (not covered): 7 | Generated: 2026-11-17 07:44 UTC

Highlights

  • Oh My Pi v18.21.0–v18.22.0 introduces breaking changes: binary analysis moves to the dsm namespace, ida.* settings are replaced by disassembler.*, legacy standalone disassembler tools and PlanReviewOverlay options are removed, and the AgentSession run lifecycle is reworked with new events and methods (agent_end, agent_pause, isRunActive, wakeSources, waitForRunEnd()).
  • Claude Code hot issue #110480 reports premium seat usage limits (Team/Enterprise) are being exhausted roughly 3–5× faster on non-Fable models (Opus/Sonnet) since the week of November 9, 2026, which the reporter attributes to a metering change rather than workload shifts.
  • jcode v1.0.0 launches jcode Cloud (/cloud moves a session or swarm to a VM, /local brings it back), reworks swarms to plan in phases and parallel lanes with a pinned team progress view, and claims 25% less CPU, idle wakeups down from 2.68 to 1.51/sec, and rendered-span memory in a large conversation down from 20.4 MB to 14.6 MB.

Coding Agents & Assistants

Claude Code

  • Release: v2.1.326 fixes cp being refused when only the file's source was covered by an Edit deny rule, fixes Bash commands that delete or overwrite files (find -delete, cat a > b, sort -o) being summed up in the transcript as a search or a read, fixes a misleading "Dangerous rm operation" warning in the Bash permission prompt on commands with no rm, and fixes background sessions losing the LLM gateway their shell exported — after a crash, a reopen from another folder, or when the background service lacks it — so they now stop before any model request, plus the background service ending the user's own processes, such as an SSH login, when a process number on its list had been reused by another user's process. It also starts sessions with agent teams enabled in Code Mode, warns at startup when a --allowedTools, --disallowedTools or --tools value has an entry that doesn't look like a complete rule, adds a /status row saying when your provider or an environment variable such as DISABLE_TELEMETRY turns features off, and adds OTEL_RESOURCE_INCLUDE_HOST (off by default) to include host.name and host.id in OpenTelemetry resource attributes.
  • News: Tokendoctor – the same Claude Code for up to 38% less — the Hacker News post presents a Claude Code plugin that shows what your use overpays, fixes it with a diff you approve, and puts any change back; it runs on your machine, and the post claims up to 38% lower cost.
  • Hot issue: #110480: an issue reports that premium seat usage limits (Team/Enterprise) are being exhausted roughly 3–5x faster on non-Fable models (Opus / Sonnet) since the week of November 9, 2026, and says everyone in the reporter's organization on premium seats sees the same drop at the same time, which the reporter attributes to a change in how non-Fable usage is metered rather than to any change in workloads, prompts, repositories or plugins. (regression; 2 comments, 2 👍; +4 in the last 24h)

OpenCode

  • Release: v1.19.6 makes OpenCode 1 offer the upgrade to OpenCode 2.0 in the desktop app, which downloads in the background and installs only when you choose Restart to upgrade, Upgrade on quit, or Later, keeping your sessions, projects and settings; the release notes say plugins made for OpenCode 1 need an update. In the core, sessions with many images no longer send oversized requests — when a session's image history passes 25 MiB, the oldest images are replaced with a placeholder — and a provider error for a request body that is too large now starts compaction and a retry instead of failing the turn.
  • Release: Alongside it, process-daemon-v0.6.0 publishes opencode-pty 0.6.0 (protocol 9) from packages/process-daemon to npm as @opencode/pty@0.6.0.
  • News: OpenCode Browse — the Hacker News post describes Browse as letting OpenCode and other MCP clients use your real browser, where agents read, click, type, take screenshots, record tabs, and hand logins and 2FA back to you.

Oh My Pi

  • Release: Across v18.21.0–v18.22.0, binary analysis moves out of the standalone ida and ghidra tools into the backend-neutral dsm namespace (xd://eval/dsm), the ida.enabled, ida.maxOpen and ida.idleCloseSec settings are replaced by disassembler.backend, disassembler.maxOpen and disassembler.idleCloseSec, and the legacy standalone disassembler tools, the Copy and Edit-in-editor buttons in the Tern plan review sheet, plus PlanReviewOverlay options in their old form are removed — options now take PlanReviewOverlayChoice objects. The same range makes TtyWriter require a drain threshold and callback and only support independently reopenable TTYs, requires terminals with output backpressure to implement onOutputDrain(callback) returning an unsubscribe function, and reworks the AgentSession run lifecycle: agent_end is emitted once when a run can no longer resume, agent_pause reports runs stopped while awaiting work, hasPendingAsyncWork(), settleAsyncWork() and suppressAutoResumeUntilPrompt() are replaced by isRunActive, wakeSources and waitForRunEnd(), and abort() now also ends runs paused on background work.
  • Release: It fixes slow streaming of Gemma tool calls with large arguments, and fixes the xAI Grok OAuth model grok-composer-2.5-fast being identified as non-reasoning, so it now supports thinking levels from minimal through xhigh.
  • Release: It adds Tern plan review editing and comments — double-click a plan to edit it, select text to add Google Docs-style comments, and send comments to Refine — Ghidra support with automatic setup of Ghidra, JDK and PyGhidra when analysis is explicitly requested, with Auto mode using an installed IDA Pro when available and falling back to Ghidra otherwise, and sharing of live analysis databases with child agents through db.handle() and dsm.open(handle). Also added are configurable automatic subagent prewalk via task.agentPrewalkAuto, automatic reasoning-capability detection with remembered effort levels for unknown models, inline image and web-page replies with interactive embedded pages in Tern replies (tui.renderEmbeds to disable the rendering), and Modal as a hosted inference provider, while the local speech model changes from Kokoro to Phonon 31M.

jcode

Highlights

  • Databricks users starting new streaming queries in real-time mode on Runtime 19 now filter late events against the live watermark and evict state sooner by default; to keep the previous behavior, set spark.databricks.streaming.realTimeMode.realTimeWatermark.enabled to false before starting the query (checkpoint restarts are unaffected).
  • Azure Databricks users ingesting PostgreSQL change data can now do so with the PostgreSQL integrated CDC pipeline (Beta), which needs no separate ingestion gateway.

Queries restarted from an existing checkpoint keep their original behavior, and to keep the previous behavior for a new query, set spark.databricks.streaming.realTimeMode.realTimeWatermark.enabled to false before starting it.
